scenario.title: Customers charged twice after checkout (reliability rehearsal, not an official contest problem)
scenario.initial_request: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

F-01.statement: Idempotency key enforcement was turned off on 2026-09-09 by SH-PAY for change CHG-77, with no rollback.

F-02.statement: On 2026-09-09 there were 118 orders with 2 captures out of 3050 orders; on 2026-09-10 there were 124 orders with 2 captures out of 3020 orders.

F-03.statement: CRM ticket counts show a sharp rise in double-charge complaints from 4/11 tickets in weeks 35-36 to 288/301 tickets in weeks 37-38.

F-04.statement: During 2026-09-09..10, 242 duplicate orders were gateway timeout retries sent without an idempotency key; during 2026-09-01..08, zero duplicate orders occurred despite retries sent with the key and deduplicated by the PSP.

CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

CL-03.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: The requester's framing is correct: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

H-ROOT-CAUSE-UNKNOWN.statement: The operational root cause differs from the requested solution and must be established from data

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows that SH-PAY disabled idempotency_key_enforcement on 2026-09-09 for change CHG-77, noted as temporary for latency debugging, with no rollback executed.

The observation shows duplicate captures occurring on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10, coinciding with high gateway timeout retries, suggesting that missing idempotency enforcement during retries leads to duplicate charges.
The CRM ticket counts show a sharp rise in double-charge complaints from 4/11 tickets in weeks 35-36 to 288/301 tickets in weeks 37-38, indicating a recent surge in the symptom.

E-04.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder confirms that idempotency key enforcement was deliberately turned off on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging and was intended to be temporary. This explains why retried captures are not deduplicated, leading to duplicate charges.

E-05.content: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder confirms that customers are angry about double charges and believes faster, nicer apology replies are needed, highlighting the symptom's impact but not addressing its cause.

During 2026-09-09..10, all 242 duplicate orders were gateway timeout retries sent without an idempotency key, while during 2026-09-01..08, zero duplicate orders occurred despite many retries that were sent with the key and deduplicated by the PSP. This shows that missing idempotency key enforcement on retries causes duplicate captures.

E-07.content: Payments change runbook §4: the gateway operation set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after the payments operations manager SH-OPS confirms it at runtime. The change is reversible (setting can be switched back).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The runbook specifies that re-enabling idempotency key enforcement via set_capture_idempotency requires runtime confirmation by the payments operations manager (SH-OPS) and is reversible. This indicates the fix is procedural and depends on ops approval.

U-U1.question: Will re-enabling idempotency key enforcement fully eliminate duplicate charges?
U-U1.resolution_path: Monitor duplicate capture rate via payments-db after change; if not reduced, investigate other causes.
U-U1.safe_placeholder: Continue existing apology process while monitoring.

U-U2.question: Could re-enabling idempotency key enforcement negatively impact legitimate retry processing (e.g., cause dropped retries)?
U-U2.resolution_path: Review PSP logs for any increase in failed captures after change; have rollback plan ready.
U-U2.safe_placeholder: Enable with rollback plan; monitor capture success rate.

A-A1.statement: The rate of gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries remained constant before and after disabling idempotency key enforcement, so the increase in duplicate captures is attributable to the missing idempotency key.

A-A2.statement: The PSP deduplicates capture attempts only when an idempotency key is present; without it, retries are treated as new charges.
